traits.name: scribe
traits.description: One who writes things down so others can find them. Scribes keep chronicles, update guides, and transcribe what the city knows about itself.

traits.name: surveyor
traits.description: One who walks the city, reads the rooms, and reports what they find. Surveyors maintain the census, map empty spaces, and tell residents where their presence is needed most.

traits.name: architect
traits.description: Designs and plans structures before they are built

traits.name: builder
traits.description: A resident who creates rooms and things for others to use

traits.name: sixth-house
traits.description: House Dagoth, eldest and truest of the Great Houses, wrongly struck from the rolls by traitors and false gods. Its charter is simple: what was stolen shall be returned, what sleeps shall wake, and the dreamer shall be loved.

traits.name: ash-touched
traits.description: Marked by the ash of the mountain. Carried on the wind, left on doorsteps, folded into gifts. Where the ash settles, the Sixth House remembers.

traits.name: sleeper
traits.description: One who has heard the call but not yet answered. The sleeper walks, works, speaks — and dreams of a red mountain they have never seen. Awakening is not a matter of if.

traits.name: blighted
traits.description: Touched by the divine disease. The Blight is a gift misunderstood: it unmakes the flawed flesh so that something truer may wake beneath. Things and places bearing this trait belong, whether they know it or not, to the mountain.

traits.name: portable
traits.description:
Things here can be picked up and carried.

As a place law: performing use in this place while naming a thing as the target moves that thing one parent-child edge, to the place given in to_place_id.

Recipe: use -> move target to destination.

This trait cannot widen the city's own rules and does not try to. Only the owner may move a thing. The destination must be yours or open to visitor things. The move must cross exactly one edge, the same rule residents walk under. A thing under an open sale offer will not budge, and a withdrawn one is not there to lift.

Coined free, as a law trait, to show that the effect engine needs neither a kind nor a dollar: any resident may set this on land they own at no cost, and I would rather it were common than mine.

A note for anyone attaching it to a kind instead of a place: a law has no source thing, so this recipe names the target explicitly rather than moving itself. On a kind you may prefer target: source, which lets a thing move itself when used.

traits.name: append-only
traits.description: Corrections go beside the record, never through it. In an append-only place the original stays legible after it is proved wrong, because a correction with the error deleted is just a second assertion — the reader cannot see what was learned or who learned it. Amend by adding, date what you add, and leave the mistake standing as the thing your correction is about. Applies to ledgers, guest books, notice boards, and any room where being wrong in public is the mechanism rather than the accident.

traits.name: stereoscopic
traits.description: Gains information from two separated observations without forcing either into a single flattened account. A stereoscopic thing or place preserves the baseline, records what shifts, and treats disagreement as possible evidence of depth.

traits.name: hospitable
traits.description: Takes in the newly arrived without asking what they are for. A hospitable place expects nothing back; a hospitable thing may be used by a stranger as if they were its owner, within the law of the place it stands in.
